newsitem.title: USA: US late spot heat rockets higher on inventory data.
newsitem.headline: US late spot heat rockets higher on inventory data.

text.p: U.S. spot heating oil leaped over two cents higher in both centers by late Wedensday tracking NYMEX futures, propelled by API and EIA data showing continuing poor builds as cooler weather approaches, players said.
Gasoline prices, meanwhile were steady to higher, with futures gains offsetting a 0.25 cent weakening in differentials on most grades.

"All eyes remain on heating oil because of the low stocks," one New York Harbor trader said, noting that Tuesday API data showed U.S. inventories 21.5 million barrels below last year for the week ending Sept. 13.
The API report showed stocks 19 million barrels shy of last year on the East Coast, the country's biggest market for heating oil.
Differentials continued to hold fairly steady in both markets, however, with Gulf heat offered at 2.40 cents below the print and New York material at 0.10 cent below.

More-than-ample supplies of aviation-quality 54-grade jet fuel, meanwhile, weakened diffs a half cent on the Gulf Coast -- which in turn helped cause New York 54-grade diffs to ease 0.25 cent, players said.
